item.title: PM believes Government has numbers for proposed constitutional changes
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka believes the Government currently has the numbers required to secure the two-third parliamentary support needed for proposed constitutional changes. While responding to fijivillage News on whether he is confident in securing two-thirds support for a bill to amend the Constitution, Rabuka said, “At the moment, yes.”
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka believes the Government currently has the numbers required to secure the two-third parliamentary support needed for proposed constitutional changes.

While responding to fijivillage News on whether he is confident in securing two-thirds support for a bill to amend the Constitution, Rabuka said, “At the moment, yes.”

When asked on the proposed constitutional amendment that would limit a Prime Minister to two terms, and would rule him out from serving as Prime Minister after the next elections, Rabuka says the Bill will be debated and voted on again.

Rabuka also clarified that the recommendations made by the Constitution Review Commission Report are not the final proposed amendments that will go before Parliament.

He says a Cabinet sub-committee has been deliberating on the CRC’s proposed amendments over the past two weeks and making changes.

The Prime Minister says those changes will be the ones that make their way to Parliament.

However, when questioned on whether there would be enough time to prepare for and hold the next general elections under a new Constitution if the proposed changes come into effect by December 24th, Rabuka, says if the Constitution is changed, transition provisions will determine which Constitution or electoral law the election will be held under.

When asked why the constitutional changes were being pursued now rather than during the Government’s first or second year in office, Rabuka says an attempt was made in the second year but it was defeated in Parliament.

He says the matter was then referred to the Supreme Court and the process has continued.

Rabuka also rejected suggestions that the constitutional review process is being rushed.

He says he and the leadership of the National Federation Party have been talking about changing the Constitution since after 2013.

item.title: Savusavu residents to raise climate concerns directly with Kamikamica at FMA Town Hall
item.description: Savusavu residents will have the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he will attend the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues tomorrow. The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum will be held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu from 7pm to 9.30pm tomorrow.
item.content:encoded:
Savusavu residents will have the chance to put their concerns directly to Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica when he will attend the Fijian Media Association Public Town Hall Forum on climate change and environmental issues tomorrow.

The Pre-COP31 Climate Change Town Hall Forum will be held at Nukubalavu Village in Savusavu from 7pm to 9.30pm tomorrow.

The forum, organised by the FMA, will give residents an opportunity to raise concerns about environmental and climate challenges affecting their communities, question Government action and propose practical solutions.

Kamikamica will be joined by Permanent Secretary for the Ministry of Environment Dr Sivendra Michael, other Government officials and experts from regional agencies who will be in Savusavu for the PINA Media Summit.

The discussion will be moderated by fijivillage News Director Vijay Narayan and Fiji Television Manager News Stella Taoi.

Residents are encouraged to share their own experiences, including changes they have observed, challenges affecting their livelihoods and solutions they believe should receive greater attention.

Questions around Government responses and the support needed by communities will also form part of the discussion.

The forum will be livestreamed across participating media platforms, including fijivillage.

It will be held alongside the 8th Pacific Media Summit, hosted by the Fijian Media Association and the Pacific Islands News Association.

The town hall is aimed at bringing community voices into the regional gathering of Pacific journalists and media leaders, while creating a direct platform for public discussion and accountability on climate and environmental issues.

The event is supported by PACMAS and forms part of the Fijian Media Association’s collaborative town hall initiative involving Fiji’s media organisations.

Residents of Savusavu and surrounding communities are being invited to attend and take part in the discussion.

item.title: Bus Operators call for urgent reinstatement of 22.5% govt support
item.description: Association President Nisar Ali Shah says with fuel prices continuing to remain high and the possibility of further increases, they believe urgent consideration is required to reinstate the support to help operators maintain sustainable and reliable public transport services. He says they made a formal submission to the Fiji Competition and Consumer Commission seeking consideration of the reinstat
item.content:encoded:
Association President Nisar Ali Shah says with fuel prices continuing to remain high and the possibility of further increases, they believe urgent consideration is required to reinstate the support to help operators maintain sustainable and reliable public transport services.

He says they made a formal submission to the Fiji Competition and Consumer Commission seeking consideration of the reinstatement of the 22.5 percent support and is currently awaiting a response.

Ali further says bus industry provides an essential public transport service to the people of Fiji.

He says operators are working to maintain services despite the increasing fuel costs, but the continued escalation in fuel prices is creating significant challenges for the sustainability of bus operations.

Ali stresses if operators are unable to sustain their operations, the impact will ultimately be felt by the travelling public.

The Association has called a meeting of its members next Wednesday to discuss the ongoing fuel crisis and its impact on the bus industry.

The Association says they will also seek to engage with Government, the FCCC and other relevant authorities to identify an urgent and sustainable way forward for the bus industry.

Ali adds the Association remains committed to working constructively with Government and the relevant authorities to ensure that the bus industry can continue providing safe, reliable and affordable public transport services to the people of Fiji.
